common: The numbers that turn stats into strength, speed and spring are ours, anchored so a 70 kg athlete with base 100 lands an elite human mark; every constant and its source is in the open in lib/games/constants.ts.

formula.0: The Pokémon Race's model, unchanged: top speed = base Speed ÷ 10 m/s, a Furusawa–Hill sprint start (τ from weight and Attack), a fade after 150 m from HP, integrated with RK4.
formula.1: Reaction to the gun: {fast}–{slow} s from Speed, seeded; under {falseStart} s is a false start and a disqualification (World Athletics TR 16).
formula.2: A dip at the line: an upright sprinter's torso crosses {dip} × its height ahead of its hips.
formula.3: Times to 1/100 s rounded up; a tie split by the photo finish at 1/1000 s.

sprint.heats: Heats and a final in the Games (the Race's knockout)

formula.0: Water speed = {vRef} m/s × (Speed/100)^{speedExp} × an aquatic factor.
formula.1: Aquatic factor: Water types and the Water 1/2/3 egg groups {water}; Fire, Rock and Ground types {sinkers} (they sink or hate water); everyone else {other}; a fish- or fin-shaped body × {fin}.
formula.2: Swift Swim doubles Speed (its real effect), only with the rain on.
formula.3: The start: a reaction, a dive (speed from Attack), a glide; stamina fades after {fade} m from HP.
formula.3turn: The start: a reaction, a dive (speed from Attack), a glide; stamina fades after {fade} m from HP; a flip turn at 50 m and a push-off from Attack.

swim.inputs: Speed, Attack, HP, weight, length, types, egg groups, Swift Swim and body shape.

modelled.1: Big bodies reach further at the start and the turn

formula.0: Run-up: the Pokémon Race's sprint model over {runUp} m, × {boardKeep} at the board (jumpers lose about 5% planting).
formula.1: Take-off: vertical speed {v} m/s × √(Attack/100) × (kg/70)^(−1/6) for bodies over 70 kg (heavy bodies get less spring per kg; lighter ones get no extra, Borelli's law).
formula.2: Flight: a projectile from the centre of mass at take-off ({comTakeoff} × height) to touchdown ({comLanding} × height), plus a take-off and a landing distance of {share} × height each.
formula.3: The board: the toe lands behind the line by a seeded amount (more scatter the faster and bigger you are); over it is a foul, about one jump in ten. Measured from the line, to the centimetre below.

long-jump.inputs: Speed, Attack, HP (stamina), weight, height and body shape.

modelled.2: Fouls and the distance lost behind the board
modelled.3: Three attempts, best counts, ties on the second best
modelled.4: Fliers and Levitate jump too: gliding isn't allowed, so the same physics

formula.0: Clearance = centre of mass at take-off ({com} × height) + rise v²/2g + technique.
formula.2: Technique: a Fosbury flop for bipeds (+{bonus} m: the bar can pass above the centre of mass); four legs or a serpent's body {penalty} m.
formula.3: The bar rises 5 cm at a time, then 3 cm when three or fewer are left; three failures in a row and you're out; ties by countback (failures at the last height, then in all), a jump-off for first.

high-jump.inputs: Attack, weight, height and body shape.

modelled.0: Tall Pokémon start high: their centre of mass is already metres up
modelled.2: World Athletics' high jump rules and countback

not.0: The approach's curve and speed (they don't change the result here)

formula.0: Release speed {v} m/s × √(Attack/100) × (kg/70)^(1/6): big bodies get a little extra from leverage.
formula.1: Capped by the shot's mass ({mass} kg): Hill's force–velocity relation slows a muscle as the load nears its strength (its best clean & jerk), and no limb swings an implement faster than {cap} m/s.
formula.2: Released at {angle}° from {share} × height (at most {releaseCap} m), with air drag on a {diameter} cm sphere.
formula.3: No arms (body shape): a head or tail flick at {noArms}% of the speed.

shot-put.inputs: Attack, Defence (through the lift), weight, height and body shape.

modelled.0: Projectile with drag, integrated in 1/600 s steps
modelled.1: Too weak to lift the shot: no mark

formula.0: Release speed = {runKeep} × the race model's speed after a {runUp} m run-up + arm speed {arm} m/s × √(Attack/100) × (kg/70)^(1/6), under the same caps as the shot.
formula.1: Flight: drag and lift on an {mass} g javelin (Hubbard & Rust, 1984), released at {angle}° from {share} × height.

javelin.inputs: Speed, Attack, weight, height and body shape.

modelled.2: The limb-speed cap: strong throwers bunch near it, height decides

not.0: The javelin's pitching (it flies nose along its path)

formula.0: Best lift = {ref} kg × (kg/70)^(2/3) × (Attack/100) × (Defence/100)^{defExp}: muscle force grows with mass^(2/3), the allometric rule behind the Sinclair coefficients.
formula.1: Three attempts in the IWF's rising-bar order: open at {opening}%, then about {second}%, then {third}%; a miss repeats the weight.
formula.2: Each lift succeeds with a chance that falls quickly above the day's best (a logistic {width}% wide).
formula.3: Real plates in 1 kg steps (IWF colours) on a 20 kg bar with 2.5 kg collars; lighter bars for light lifts.

modelled.0: A heavy Pokémon is strong but not proportionally stronger
modelled.1: Pound for pound (lift ÷ bodyweight) as its own award

formula.0: Push = {push} N × kg^(2/3) × Attack/100; brace = {brace} N × kg^(2/3) × Defence/100 + {friction} × its weight in friction.
formula.1: The bout: both charge (momentum from Speed and mass), lock up, and whoever's push beats the other's brace drives the pair back; seeded surges swing it; stamina comes from HP.
formula.2: Out of the ring (a sumo dohyō, {ring} m across, or bigger for a giant) loses; after {maxTime} s, the one pushed further back does.

wrestling.inputs: Attack, Defence, Speed, HP and weight.

modelled.0: A knockout bracket seeded by push + brace

not.0: Moves, throws or battle damage (that's Mass Battle): pure strength and mass

formula.0: Points per event from World Athletics' combined-events formula: A·(B − T)^C for times, A·(M − B)^C for marks.
formula.1: The real decathlon constants for the 100 m, 400 m, long jump, high jump, shot put and javelin; ours, of the same form, for the 200 m, the lift and the swims (1,000 points at an elite mark).
formula.2: The best all-rounder is the Champion of the Games.

modelled.0: Ten events with marks (wrestling is head to head)

not.0: Event order or fatigue across events
